stem:
Rina keeps a money plant on her balcony with soil, air, water, and sunlight. Insects visit the plant. She asks how living beings and non-living parts keep this small system in balance.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Balance is kept because living things and non-living parts work together: the plant uses sunlight and water, insects take nectar, and soil organisms return nutrients.
Only living things matter; soil, sunlight, and water play no part.
Balance would stay the same if all water and sunlight were removed.
Balance means only that the plant and insects share the same place.

teacher.key_rationale: Living beings depend on one another and on non-living parts. Plants, animals, decomposers, land, air, and water work together. Dropping non-living parts or removing water and sunlight breaks that balance.
